question: On 20 October 2026, Libya’s House of Representatives approved the illegal Türkiye-Libya Memorandum of Understanding on the delimitation of maritime jurisdictions in the Mediterranean Sea1. This development marks the agreement between Libya’s two rival authorities on the deal with Türkiye.
The EU has repeatedly noted that the memorandum violates the sovereign rights of Member States, contravenes the Law of the Sea and has no legal effect2.

Meanwhile, the Union is funding programmes on both sides of the Libyan divide, with a bilateral allocation of EUR 224 million for the period 2021-20273 through the NDICI-Global Europe financial instrument and an additional EUR 25 million that was recently announced to expand cooperation with the authorities in eastern Libya4.

The European Court of Auditors has also highlighted weaknesses in the evaluation and supervision of European actions in the country5. In view of the above, can the Vice-President of the Commission / High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy answer the following: 1.
What specific diplomatic and political initiatives will the EU take towards Libya and Türkiye to uphold international law and the sovereign rights of Member States?
What amounts have been committed and disbursed in western and eastern Libya, who are the final recipients and has the effectiveness of these funds been assessed?
Does she intend to review financial and operational cooperation with the Libyan authorities involved, ensuring the continuation of humanitarian aid given recent developments?
